introduction: Phase changes do not always follow the standard Solid -> Liquid -> Gas sequence. Some substances skip the liquid phase entirely. Furthermore, modern science recognizes two extreme states of matter beyond the classic three.

core_concepts.title: Sublimation and Deposition
core_concepts.description:
1. Sublimation: The direct conversion of a Solid into a Gas without ever becoming a liquid. (Examples: Camphor/Kapur, Naphthalene balls, Iodine, Ammonium Chloride). 
2. Deposition: The reverse process, where a Gas converts directly into a Solid without becoming a liquid (e.g., frost forming on a cold window).

core_concepts.title: Evaporation vs. Boiling
core_concepts.description:
1. Boiling is a 'Bulk Phenomenon' that happens at a specific, fixed temperature (Boiling Point). Bubbles form throughout the liquid. 
2. Evaporation is a 'Surface Phenomenon' that happens at ANY temperature below the boiling point. Evaporation always causes COOLING (because the evaporating surface particles absorb heat energy from their surroundings to escape).

core_concepts.title: The 4th State: Plasma
core_concepts.description:
Plasma consists of super-energetic and super-excited ionized gases. 
Occurrence: It exists at extremely high temperatures. The sun and the stars glow because of the presence of plasma in them. On Earth, it is artificially created in neon sign bulbs and fluorescent tubes.

core_concepts.title: The 5th State: Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC)
core_concepts.description:
Formed by cooling a gas of extremely low density (about one-hundred-thousandth the density of normal air) to super-low temperatures (near Absolute Zero). 
Significance: Predicted mathematically by Satyendra Nath Bose and Albert Einstein in 1920. Achieved experimentally in 1995.

important_entities.name: Dry Ice
important_entities.significance: A favorite question in Railway and PCS exams! Solid CO2 is called 'Dry Ice' because it does not melt into a wet liquid; it directly sublimes into carbon dioxide gas at normal atmospheric pressure. It is widely used as a refrigerant.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: If you increase humidity, does evaporation speed up? FALSE. Evaporation INCREASES with: Surface area, Temperature, and Wind speed. But it DECREASES with an increase in Humidity (because the air is already saturated with moisture).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: C - Camphor, A - Ammonium Chloride, N - Naphthalene, I - Iodine. These are the four standard examples asked in MCQs.

exam_strategy_tips: NDA/CDS Question: 'Why does water kept in an earthen pot (matka) become cold during summer?' Answer: Due to the continuous evaporation of water seeping through the microscopic pores of the pot, which draws latent heat away from the remaining water.
